text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.
GERMANY - The German debt market was closed for a holiday. Regular trading will resume on Friday. The market rose on Wednesday as December Bund futures set a new contract high.

BRITAIN - Gilts faded in the afternoon session and the day's hefty gains evaporated ahead of the close, profit-taking before the U.S. non-farm payroll on Friday was held responsible, with jitters predicted on Friday. The September long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-25/32, down 09/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French December bond futures surged to their fifth new contract high in seven sessions before profit taking in the U.S. bond market knocked them off their new-found perch, analysts said the French market continued to be buoyed by domestic demand for bonds as the relatively high bid-to-cover ratio at Thursday's Treasury auction of government bonds demonstrated. The September notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 125.40, up 0.04 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt futures soared to a record December Liffe contract high of 124.13 in a frenzy of buying before tumbling by more than 100 basis points as foreign investors rushed to take profits, dealers said a slightly easier lira gainst the mark, reflecting dollar weakness, helped to unnerve investors in late afternoon trading. The September bond future on LIFFE was trading at 123.35, up 0.05 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries erased early gains and slipped lower by midday as players took some profits before Friday's release of the influential monthly U.S. employment report. The September Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-08/32, down 02/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.85 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese Goverment Bonds (JGB) futures ended Tokyo higher, pushed up by falls in short-term interest rates. Key three-month CD rate fell to 0.52 percent, its lowest level since December 1995, and two-year interest swap rate fell in response to active purchases by some city banks. In after hours trading the September future on LIFFE was trading at 122.66, up 0.46 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market started the early Thursday session subdued, with issuance capped by a holiday in Germany and the outcome of September's U.S. jobs data on Friday. American Express unit set a $125 million five-year FRN. Depfa set a 1.0 bln French franc two-year FRN/fixed bond. F van Lanschot Bankiers launched a 300 million guilder bond. Meanwhile a Russian official said on Wednesday it would stick to its plans to issue the first tranche of its Eurobond later this year when it received a credit rating.
